# Architecture Overview

```

CelesTrak GP endpoint                    CelesTrak SATCAT dump
  gp.php?GROUP=|CATNR=                     /pub/satcat.csv
        │                                        │
        └───────────────┬────────────────────────┘
                        ▼
             CelesTrak Compliance Shield
   ├─ identifying User-Agent
   ├─ daily volume budget (halt before the request)
   ├─ cache check (2h for GP, 24h for SATCAT)
   ├─ conditional ETag request (Hash → If-None-Match → Response:304 NotModified → reuses cache)
   └─ fail-fast status gate (only 200/304; never retry anything else)
                        │
        ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
        ▼               ▼               ▼
   data/bronze/    data/sds/    data/bronze_satcat/   ← raw, byte-for-byte      ⎫
     *.csv          *.sds            *.csv             + .meta.json sidecars    ⎪
        │                               │                                       ⎪
        ▼                               ▼                                       ⎪ Bronze
   bronze_parquet/            bronze_satcat_parquet/  ← ingest_date=/hour=      ⎪
        │                               │                                       ⎪
        ▼                               ▼                                       ⎪
   bronze.raw_gp                 bronze.raw_satcat    ← idempotent load     ⎫   ⎭
        │                               │               to Postgres         ⎪
        ▼                               ▼                     ⎫             ⎪            
dbt: stg_celestrak_gp          dbt: stg_celestrak_satcat      ⎪ Staging     ⎪
        │                               │                     ⎭             ⎪
        ▼                               ▼                     ⎫             ⎪
dbt: silver.elset               dbt: silver.space_object      ⎪ Silver      ⎪ Postgres
(dedup + SCD-2)                   (dedup to current)          ⎭             ⎪
        │                               │                                   ⎪
        └───────────────┬───────────────┘                                   ⎪
                        ▼  dbt: gold                                        ⎪   ⎫
        gold.dim_object  ◀── gold.fact_propagatable_elset                   ⎪   ⎪
                        │                                                   ⎪   ⎪ Gold
                        ▼  sat-tracker-propagate (SGP4 + TEME→WGS84)        ⎪   ⎪
              gold.position_snapshot         ← PostGIS, GIST indexed        ⎭   ⎭ 
```

## Ingestion
- I'm ingesting the GP OMM data (the elements describing the orbits; facts; Format: CSV + binary SDS;) selectable by group and catalogue number and the SATCAT data (immutable properties of the Satellites; dimensions, Format: CSV) as a complete dump from their respective endpoints on CelesTrak
- Due to their compliance policies I use a very strict regime for ingests, i.e. conditional ETag requests (Data is only fetched if Server acknowledges it is new) otherwise previously cached data is used from the expected refresh intervals (2h for GP, 24h for SATCAT), no retries

## CLI
- there are CLI functions for every step of the pipeline (GP extraction, SATCAT extraction, loading, transformation, propagation) which makes it easy to propagate the data downstream and provides an interface for orchestration later with Airflow (locally) or StepFunctions

## Bronze layer
The data is saved as raw csv and with ingestion information in separate json files as source of truth for reprocucability and auditability
After that data is partitioned and converted into parquet via pyarrow so its queryable more efficiently and to be staged and typed in postgres with lineage columns ingest_ts, ingestion_id, source, source_file, target

## Silver layer
The data is curated, i.e. deduplicated
- for elset a scd-2 history is created with a window function
- for satcat the rows are also deduped which brings it to a current state
- plausibility tests for angles, dedup and scd2

## Gold layer

Here the two data sets are joined as a view and enriched with derived information
- is_decayed: if decay_date is not NULL
- is_earth_orbiting: from orbit_center column
- orbit_regime: catagorical: 2000 (LEO) < 35000 (MEO) < GEO/HEO  

## Propagation
 - I used a py-library SGP4 to transform the element sets into fixed positions and velocities in space in (x,y,z) coordinates with earth center as point of origin, to translate these coordinates into lon, lat, alt to make them visible on a map I used a couple of mathematical rotations and formulasbut wrote them myself
 - The coordinates then land together with additional informations like velocity and norad_cat_id only for the newest epoch (snaphot) in a PostGIS db that provides geospatial indexing and is already able to show the positions on a map
